sam: Heads-up — onboarding pegasus7b-lite. Ran an int4 quant smoke and seeing a subtle quality regression on long-context summarization vs fp16 baseline. Outputs diverge after ~250 tokens. Suspect rotary/kv cache alignment or vocab mapping problem. Repro below.

sam: Repro (local):

```
# convert -> quant -> smoke
python tools/convert_model.py --src pegasus7b/fp16 --out pegasus7b/int4 --format gemma-converter \
  && python tools/quantize.py --model pegasus7b/int4 --cfg int4-config.yaml \
  && pytest tests/smoke/test_long_summarize.py::test_200tok -k pegasus7b
```

sam: Log snippet:
```
[2024-06-05 14:12:08] INFO: generation started
[2024-06-05 14:12:11] WARN: rotary_scale_mismatch head=3 expected=1.0 got=0.996
[2024-06-05 14:12:12] ERROR: token_id_remap detected gap at id 50257 -> 50256
[2024-06-05 14:12:12] INFO: divergence_point token=\"the\" idx=257
```

chen: Can you paste the model hash / converter commit? Also which tokenizer did you use (pegasus-native vs shared-qwen)?

sam: model_hash: sha256:abc123... (uploaded to /artifacts/pegasus7b/1718341122). Converter commit: gemma-converter@3f9b2c1. Tokenizer: pegasus-native v1.2. Did try shared-qwen briefly — similar but not identical.

maria: Two quick hypotheses:
  1) embed projection ordering (proj weight transpose) — we've seen that when switching converter codepaths.
  2) tokenizer casing/canonicalization — pegasus has weird soft-hyphen tokens that sometimes collapse in shared tokenizers.

raj: Also check KV cache index wraparound / prefix cache reuse. If token ids shifted by one in the converter, the rotary sin/cos alignment will be off headwise. Try headwise rotary normalization dump.

sam: Running a quick headwise rotary dump now: `python tools/inspect_rotary.py --model artifacts/pegasus7b/1718341122 --dump headwise.csv`

dev-bot: CI job launched: quant-smoke/pegasus7b/1718341122 — https://ci.redwood/quant-smoke/1718341122 (status: running)

chen: If you can run `python tools/convert_vocab_mapping.py --src-tokenizer pegasus-native --target-tokenizer shared-qwen --check-rotary` that will highlight any token id aliasing/soft-hyphen collisions.

sam: Ran that. Short output:
```
checked 50288 tokens
soft-hyphen collisions: 7 -> examples: 0x202A (\u202A) maps to id 31245 vs 31246
rotary-phase-delta mean=0.0009 std=0.0017
headwise-signflip count=0 for 64 heads
```

maria: Phase delta small but nonzero. The token collisions are suspicious — even a handful of aliased tokens can cause drift early in long-context generation. Can you run one sample with explicit `--pad-sentinel 1` and compare logits at token 256? Use `--logit-diff` flag.

sam: Did that. Logit diff at idx 256 between fp16 and int4-converted: `L2=0.42, max=3.8` — concentrated on a handful of tokens (soft-hyphen variants). Attached small CSV to artifact.

raj: Sounds like a vocab aliasing + tiny rotary phase leak that amplifies in long context. Short-term fix: add an explicit token remap to preserve canonical pegasus token ids during conversion. Also try `--rotary-unify` option in gemma-converter which forces canonical phase tables.

sam: Tried `--rotary-unify` + remap. Smoke now passes basic fuzzers; qualitative samples look closer. Still want a deeper eval on SummEval across 1k prompts. Kicked off a job.

maria: For tracking: open an onboarding ticket with steps, artifacts, and a small patch to converter that applies the remap + rotary-unify. Label: onb/pegasus7b, priority=P2.

sam: Will open the ticket and assign to @chen and @raj. Summary in ticket: "pegasus7b-lite: token aliasing (soft-hyphens) caused rotor phase mismatch after gemma-converter int4 path; mitigated with remap + rotary-unify; running full eval." Will post link when created.

chen: Nice triage. If the eval passes, we should add a conversion test that checks for any token id collisions against the canonical pegasus vocab (fail the conversion if >0 collisions).

sam: Agree. Action items: 1) ticket + artifacts (sam), 2) converter test (chen), 3) full SummEval run and threshold check (raj). Ping me if jobs fail. :thumbsup:

raj: I'll watch the SummEval run. If it drifts again after 1k tokens, we may need to adjust quant zero-point handling per-head.

dev-bot: CI update: quant-smoke/pegasus7b/1718341122 (job #42) status: passed

sam: Awesome — will proceed to dedicate a small rollout to staging with canary=5%.
